text: On that day you will say: "I thank you, LORD. Though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away, and you have comforted me.
See, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the LORD, the LORD himself, is my strength and my song; he has become my salvation."
With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.

versions.text: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
versions.explanation: מַעְיָן denotes a spring or fountain of living water rather than a dug well (בְּאֵר). "Springs" is more accurate and keeps the image of flowing, life-giving water.

text: On that day you will say: "Give thanks to the LORD, call on his name; make known among the peoples what he has done, proclaim that his name is exalted.

versions.text: On that day you will say: "Give thanks to the LORD, call on his name; make known among the nations what he has done, proclaim that his name is exalted.
versions.explanation: בָעַמִּים is "among the peoples"; "nations" normally renders גּוֹיִם. Using "peoples" keeps the distinction consistent and is equally natural for oral reading.

text: Sing to the LORD, for he has done glorious things; let this be known in all the earth.
Shout aloud and sing for joy, you who dwell in Zion, for the Holy One of Israel is great in your midst."

versions.text: Shout aloud and sing for joy, you who dwell in Zion, for great among you is the Holy One of Israel."
versions.explanation: בְּקִרְבֵּךְ means "in your midst" (dwelling within), not "among you," which in English can suggest one great figure within a group of comparable persons. "In your midst" preserves the sense of God's presence inside the city and reads smoothly aloud.
